Let's wrap the next output in a `DT::datatable()` function to make it more readable: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} DT::datatable(airlines) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: # mutating joins ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} band |> left_join(instrument, by = "name") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 3 × 3 name band plays 1 Mick Stones 2 John Beatles guitar 3 Paul Beatles bass ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} band |> right_join(instrument, by = "name") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 3 × 3 name band plays 1 John Beatles guitar 2 Paul Beatles bass 3 Keith guitar ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} band |> full_join(instrument, by = "name") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 4 × 3 name band plays 1 Mick Stones 2 John Beatles guitar 3 Paul Beatles bass 4 Keith guitar ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} band |> inner_join(instrument, by = "name") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 3 name band plays 1 John Beatles guitar 2 Paul Beatles bass ``` ::: ::: ## Your Turn 1 Which airlines had the largest arrival delays? Complete the code below. 1. Join `airlines` to `flights` 2. Compute and order the average arrival delays by airline. Display full names, no codes. *(Hint: Be sure to remove each `_` before turning eval to true)* ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flights |> filter(!is.na(arr_delay)) |> __________________ |> group_by(_________) |> __________________ |> arrange(__________) ``` ::: ## Your Turn 2 Join `flights` and `airports` by `dest` and `faa`. Then for each `name`, compute the `distance` from NYC and the average `arr_delay`. *Hint: use `first()` to get the first value of distance.* Order by average delay, worst to best. *(Hint: Be sure to remove each `_` before turning eval to true)* ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flights |> filter(!is.na(arr_delay)) |> ______(airports, __________________) |> group_by(name) |> _________(distance = _____________, delay = _____________) |> ______(_____(delay)) ``` ::: # filtering joins ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} band |> semi_join(instrument, by = "name") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 2 name band 1 John Beatles 2 Paul Beatles ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} band |> anti_join(instrument, by = "name") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 × 2 name band 1 Mick Stones ``` ::: ::: ## Your Turn 3 How many airports in `airports` are serviced by flights in `flights`? (i.e. how many places can you fly to direct from New York?) Notice that the column to join on is named `faa` in the **airports** data set and `dest` in the **flights** data set. *(Hint: Be sure to remove each `_` before turning eval to true)* ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} __________ |> _____________________________ |> select(faa) ``` ::: # Take aways * `left_join()` retains all cases in _left_ data set * `right_join()` retains all cases in _right_ data set * `full_join()` retains all cases in _either_ data set * `inner_join()` retains _only_ cases in _both_ data sets * `semi_join()` extracts cases that _have_ a match * `anti_join()` extracts cases that _do not have_ a match
